newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed slightly higher at midday on Tuesday in extremely dull pre-Christmas trade.
January 2023s were up 24 bp to 112.51/71 but dealers said the rise was due to very thin volumes rather than any fundamentals.
Dealers said institutional players were inactive, with most merely closing their books and tidying their desks.
"The only ones doing anything in the market are a few retail customers, but the volume is almost nil," one dealer said. Dealers expect volumes on Friday to be just as quiet.
"Without anything new, there will be even less trade than today," one said.
Next Monday, the Dutch state will announce its bond issue plans for the 1997 first quarter, which may give the market some fresh impetus.

Dealers vary widely in their opinions on how much the state will want to collect through new issues. Forecasts for total first quarter bond issues range from 10 to 25 billion guilders, with little consensus on how many bonds will be issued.
Some reckon on two to four new state loans with the possibility that the state could instead raise money through its DTC (Dutch Treasury Certificate) programme and adapt its redemption scheme.
Others said the state could open a new 10-15 year-benchmark to fill the gap between the current benchmarks, adding they might also re-open older loans.
